newsitem.title: SPAIN: DIVING-PAKHALINA TURNS TABLES ON FELLOW RUSSIAN.
newsitem.headline: DIVING-PAKHALINA TURNS TABLES ON FELLOW RUSSIAN.

text.p: Yulia Pakhalina of Russia upset the form book to win the European championship women's three-metre springboard event on Sunday.
Reigning European champion Vera Ilyna started the competition as favourite but 19-year-old Pakhalina executed an excellent series of five dives to defeat her compatriot.
Carrying forward 230.07 points from her five dives in the morning's semifinal, Pakhalina finished with 567.30 points.
"It's my first major championship title so winning the gold medal hasn't really sunk in yet," a stunned Pakhalina said.
Pakhalina won the silver medal behind Ilyna at the European Championships in Vienna two years ago.
The teenager picked out her third effort of a backward 2-1/2 somersault dive as key.
"My programme depends on it. If it goes well then the rest of the dives are relatively easy. However if I have problems then doing well with my other dives becomes much harder," Pakhalina added.
She scored 57.60 with the dive in contrast to Ilyna, who could muster only 53.10 when she performed the dive in the previous round.
Two outstanding dives of a reverse 2-1/2 somersaults and a reverse 1-1/2 somersaults with 2-1/2 twists completed her series.
Pakhalina scored over 70 points on both occasions, the only diver in the competition to achieve such a high mark.
Ilyna had won the one-metre springboard title on Friday and was bitterly disappointed at having to settle for the silver this time with 524.28 points.
"I threw it away. It was my third dive that lost me the gold medal," Ilyna said.
But the 23-year-old student at the University of Texas is determined to bounce back.
"I still think I can win the world title in Perth next year," she said.
Anna Lindberg of Sweden won the bronze medal with 508.02 points.
Earlier on Sunday Russia completed a clean sweep of the synchronised swimming titles.
They added the team gold medal to the solo and duet victories achieved on Friday and Saturday respectively.
The Russian eight-woman squad scored 99.240 marks.
They were convincing gold medallists but controversy accompanied their high score which included a 10 for technical merit and four 10s for artistic interpretation.
One team member committed a poolside error in the opening sequence which rendered the routine less than perfect.
France took the silver medals with 97.400 while Italy came third with 96.240.
